headline: Government plans 900 million kroner for schools after historically weak test results
headline_short: Government plans 900 million kroner for schools
deck: 200 million kroner goes to 100 schools where pupils lag in Danish and maths; there are no plans for a teacher pay rise.
standard: The government will set aside 900 million kroner for public schools in its 2027 budget proposal, four ministers told Politiken. Of that, 200 million goes to 100 schools where pupils do particularly badly in Danish and maths, 200 million to small rural schools and 500 million to schools generally.
It follows a Pisa survey, which about a month ago found 15-year-olds historically weak in science, maths and reading.
The government wants more teachers, such as more lessons taught by two, but plans no pay rise. 'I personally think we should look elsewhere,' Mette Frederiksen, the prime minister, told DR.
Gordon Ørskov Madsen, chairman of the teachers' union, called it 'very positive'.
short: The government will set aside 900 million kroner for public schools in its 2027 budget proposal, four ministers told Politiken, 200 million of it for 100 schools where pupils do particularly badly in Danish and maths.
